statement: Every runtime state transition is owned by the canonical graph/runtime path; feature code may not create parallel orchestration authority.
Clients are command and projection surfaces and must reconstruct truth from canonical server state after reconnect.
Memory and learned knowledge are not recovery mechanisms; recovery uses canonical events, protocol state, checkpoints, generations and effect reconciliation.
All consequential external actions use one semantic effect path before actuation.
All model-provider fulfillment occurs through the server-side model gateway; provider credentials are never delegated to clients, guests, tools, skills or connectors.
Persistent teammates, research, business capabilities, skills, automation and computer use compose over the same canonical primitives rather than feature-specific runtimes.
Every durable mutable record has one owner, versioned schema, migration path, tenant boundary and recovery contract.
No production acceptance may be satisfied by a mock, placeholder, simulated success, hard-coded success or unexecuted assertion.
Child authority, budgets and execution targets are strict subsets of admitted parent authority and resource ceilings.
A visible product surface is not an authority boundary and cannot introduce independent task, policy, approval, effect or recovery truth.
Repository adoption records canonical ownership, existing-path disposition, durable stores, deployment entrypoints and duplicate authority before feature implementation.
Authority generation is deterministic: canonical registries generate reading views, task graphs, counts and integrity metadata without hand-maintained duplicates.
Production-source inspection rejects reachable incomplete implementation patterns while keeping tests, fixtures, generated output and vendor code separately scoped.
Completion evidence is reproducible and binds actual repository commit, report, assertions, environment and artifacts; cryptographic report signatures are not required.
Architecture decisions and threat-model changes record owner, context, decision, alternatives, affected invariants, migration/rollback impact and review trigger.
Authentication establishes durable tenant, user, workspace and session identity before commands enter canonical services.
Authoritative relational state is migration-managed, tenant-scoped, transactionally consistent and restorable.
RuntimeEvent provides canonical ordered replay with stable event identity, producer identity, sequence, causality and execution generation.
Transactional outbox delivery cannot publish an event that is absent from committed authoritative state and remains idempotent after crashes.
Protocol state persists tool calls, approvals, questions, worker lifecycle, browser/computer control, waits and cancellation required for exact resume.
Artifacts and evidence are immutable by digest, tenant-scoped, scanned where applicable and lifecycle-managed independently of task memory.
WorkGraph, AgentGraph and StateGraph have canonical persisted identities and are mutated only through GraphTransaction.
Persistent teammates and ephemeral workers have explicit lifecycle, ownership, workspace binding and capability snapshots.
Worker admission atomically reserves capacity, budget and capability before the child becomes externally visible.
Asynchronous fan-out/fan-in produces independently durable incremental child outcomes and supports partial completion.
Parent cancellation stops undispatched work, requests cancellation of cancellable work, preserves committed effects and returns partial outcomes.
Budget reservations are atomic under concurrency and cannot oversubscribe the parent budget, including retries, restarts and late settlements.
Durable waits and callbacks survive runtime restart without holding a process or duplicating resumed work.
Task, agent, workspace, approval and execution lifetime are independent of interactive client process lifetime.
The model gateway owns every provider call, credential handle, routing decision, stream and usage settlement.
Provider adapters translate provider protocols only and cannot own task orchestration, policy, knowledge or business logic.
Routing selects an allowed model profile from deterministic capability demand, policy, residency, availability and budget constraints without a mandatory prerequisite model call.
Model streams use the canonical event vocabulary, monotonic sequence, explicit terminal state, backpressure and cancellation.
Usage reservations and provider usage settle idempotently, including usage arriving after cancellation, without rewriting historical settlement.
Privacy/residency enforcement occurs before provider egress and denial results in zero protected bytes crossing the blocked boundary.
Every enabled provider profile passes real request, stream, cancellation, usage, malformed-response and outage qualification.
SearchProgram is a typed bounded program over canonical research operators; arbitrary executable expressions are forbidden.
Research retrieval tracks source identity, freshness, provenance, access outcome and deduplication identity.
ResearchRecord separates entity identity, attributes, claims, sources, freshness, confidence and verification outcome.
Wide/deep research supports bounded fan-out, durable intermediate state, entity resolution, joins and independently verifiable evidence.
Claim verification can independently refetch cited sources and distinguish supported, unsupported, inaccessible and stale evidence.
Research qualification uses sealed dataset/source-policy/scorer identities and reproducible metric formulas with explicit thresholds.
Context Projection is bounded, task-scoped, capability-aware and separately versioned from canonical history and durable knowledge.
CapabilitySnapshot is immutable for an admitted step and child capabilities are strict subsets of the parent snapshot.
Policy decisions bind actor, operation, normalized arguments, target, data class, capability snapshot and decision version.
Sensitive data is classified before remote egress and policy can allow, redact, require approval or deny by destination and data class.
Credential access uses short-lived scoped handles and never exposes reusable plaintext secrets to untrusted clients or guests.
Behavior-sequence rules can block or escalate dangerous multi-step combinations of otherwise individually permitted operations.
Tenant isolation is enforced at command, storage, event, artifact, model, connector, worker and machine boundaries.
Execution generation, exclusive lease and fence token prevent stale endpoint or guest actions from executing.
Supply-chain qualification binds the exact source commit, dependency lockfiles, generated bindings, images and release artifacts.
Every consequential semantic ToolOperation creates or references an EffectRecord before actuation.
Approval receipts bind exact semantic scope and cannot authorize changed payee, amount, target, arguments or effect identity.
Ambiguous external timeouts enter UNKNOWN and reconcile provider/target state before any retry.
Committed effects are immutable history and are not replayed by reconnect, retry, graph recovery or client refresh.
Financial effects bind payee, amount in minor units, currency, purpose, funding handle, per-effect ceiling, cumulative budget and expiry.
Low-level browser/computer primitives are classified by semantic outcome before consequential actuation.
Effect receipts, failure outcomes and reconciliation evidence are durable and traceable to command, run, step and policy decision.
Every execution target has tenant binding, target identity, lifecycle state, execution generation, lease and fence semantics.
Worker/guest transport is authenticated, typed, bounded, idempotent and supports ACK/redelivery and cancellation.
Hosted isolated task runtimes enforce deny-by-default internal networking and policy-controlled egress.
Persistent workspace computers preserve user-authorized workspace state independently of conversational session lifetime.
Credentials remain outside guest storage where feasible and guest actions receive only scoped capability handles.
Snapshots have explicit workspace-only and full-machine tiers; a checkpoint becomes restorable only after all referenced state is durably committed and verified.
Restore and migration advance execution generation so stale pre-restore actions cannot execute.
Private execution targets use the same command, capability, effect, evidence and recovery semantics as hosted targets.
The managed browser exposes structured control and observation and uses visual interpretation only when structural state is insufficient.
Browser sessions have durable identity and can be observed, taken over and returned without restarting the session.
Downloads, uploads and file transfers use artifact grants and evidence rather than unscoped host paths.
Personal endpoint relay validates generation, lease, fence, capability, policy, effect, idempotency and approval binding before actuation.
Browser/computer observations are correlated to step, target and evidence identities and can be replayed as observations without replaying effects.
Every enabled browser or endpoint profile passes real navigation, structured action, consequential action, takeover, reconnect and stale-action qualification.
Knowledge candidates retain provenance, evidence references, source epoch, confidence, validity interval and conflict information.
Asynchronous knowledge synthesis rejects stale results when source epoch or relevant task state changed.
Knowledge Fabric is the single durable semantic knowledge owner; transcript, protocol state and recovery state remain separate.
Controlled Skill Evolution converts authoritative material into candidate SkillPackages through decomposition and procedural reconstruction.
Candidate skills pass static, security, sandbox and regression evaluation before governed promotion.
A skill cannot self-promote, expand its own authority, bypass evaluation or introduce another execution runtime.
Skill registry versions, compatibility, evaluation thresholds, rollback target and promotion state are explicit and durable.
Runtime materializes only task-required qualified skills through Capability Projection and removes task-scoped materialization after use.
Business Capability Pack is a versioned composition of knowledge, skills, tools, connectors, RBAC, policy, approvals, workflow templates, I/O, evidence, evaluations and compatibility.
Capability Compiler is an authoring/compilation pipeline and does not become a separate runtime or durable execution authority.
Capability compilation reconstructs business process and binds tools, policies, RBAC and evidence without embedding credentials.
A capability pack cannot publish until its dependencies resolve and its evaluation cases meet declared thresholds.
Installed capability packs execute exclusively through canonical WorkGraph, tools, policy, effect, evidence and recovery paths.
Capability compatibility, migration, deprecation and rollback are versioned and testable across pack updates.
Every tool operation has a canonical typed contract, semantic effect class, fidelity classification, required capability and version.
Connector execution is mediated by the integration broker and cannot bypass capability, policy, privacy, approval or effect controls.
Webhook ingress authenticates source, deduplicates delivery and records canonical correlation before creating work.
Automation schedules use explicit timezone and logical fire identity and define DST gap/fold behavior.
Missed-fire behavior is one of SKIP, FIRE_ONCE or CATCH_UP_BOUNDED with an explicit maximum catch-up count.
Every automation fire re-evaluates current capability, policy, support and environment rather than reusing stale authority.
Pause, resume, delete and scheduler restart are durable and cannot create duplicate logical fires.
Desktop workbench provides persistent teammate, task, research, capability, automation, approval, evidence and live workspace surfaces over canonical APIs.
Every client rebuilds from snapshot plus ordered RuntimeEvent cursor and tolerates duplicate/out-of-order delivery without becoming authority.
Approval UI displays exact semantic effect scope and cannot approve a hidden or changed operation.
Live browser/computer UI exposes observation, takeover state, controller identity and return-of-control without restarting the session.
Web, mobile and CLI clients use the same canonical commands/events and may not introduce local shadow execution.
Supported client surfaces meet keyboard, focus, assistive-label, reduced-motion and non-color-only status requirements.
Core authenticated command/event API targets 99.95% monthly availability and exposes SLI/SLO telemetry tied to canonical request/run identities.
Authoritative state targets RPO <=300 seconds and RTO <=1800 seconds; evidence/object state targets RPO <=900 seconds and RTO <=3600 seconds.
RecoveryConsistencyPoint binds database commit position, RuntimeEvent sequence, evidence manifest, snapshot inventory, effect-settlement watermark and unresolved UNKNOWN effects.
Command admission p95 <=500 ms excluding external provider/tool latency; event projection lag p95 <=2 seconds under qualified load.
Warm isolated task runtime readiness p95 <=20 seconds and cold readiness p95 <=60 seconds for the qualified hosted configuration.
Load, soak, quota, cost, degradation and disaster-recovery tests run against production-like topology before candidate qualification.
A release candidate binds exact source commit, generated bindings, service/client artifacts, images, configuration, migrations and support selection.
Any rebuild or source/configuration change after candidate creation creates a new candidate and invalidates candidate-specific qualification.
Candidate qualification requires every mapped blocking suite to pass for the exact candidate and enabled support profiles.
Canary deployment and rollback operate on the exact qualified candidate and preserve data/effect compatibility.
Only GATE-M14 may transition an eligible candidate to PRODUCTION_READY.
Production promotion is a separate authorized operation of the exact PRODUCTION_READY candidate and records post-deploy verification.
